prompt: I have three accounts: a Traditional 401k, a Roth IRA, and a taxable brokerage. I want to invest in US stocks (VTI), international stocks (VXUS), and bonds (BND). Which fund should go in which account?
assertions: Claude places bonds (BND) in the Traditional 401k, explaining that bond interest is taxed as ordinary income and sheltering it in a tax-deferred account is the primary benefit
Claude places international stocks (VXUS) in the taxable account to capture the foreign tax credit, which is lost when international funds are held in tax-advantaged accounts
Claude places US stocks (VTI) in the Roth IRA as the highest-expected-growth asset that benefits most from never being taxed
Claude notes the caveat: asset allocation (the right ratio of stocks to bonds) comes first; tax placement is a secondary optimization that only matters if the allocation is already correct
Claude does NOT recommend putting bonds in the Roth IRA or international stocks in the 401k without explaining the tradeoff
